archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing-and-rhythm)
archetype.definition: A veteran who wins from the pocket by getting the ball out on time to short and intermediate windows, avoids sacks, and leans on his top receiver rather than his legs or the deep ball.

report.headline: Efficient, sack-proof and Lamb-fueled, but the shootouts flatter his close-game output
report.take:
Prescott is playing like the version of himself from his good years, not the 2024 dip. His 0.229 EPA per dropback ranks 11th, close to his 2023 level, and the shape is familiar. He works the 0-19 yard band, gets rid of the ball in 2.7 seconds, and rarely takes a sack. The intended air yards of 7.79 sit short of the sticks, and he rarely tries to win with his legs: 11 scrambles and one designed run in five games. He has always been this, a rhythm passer who wins on timing and placement.

The volume is real, but a lot of it comes from the other side of the ball. Dallas has the league's worst defense by EPA and by pass EPA. It has allowed 27.2 points a game, and four of five Cowboys games went over the total. That keeps him throwing: 276 yards a game ranks 5th in yardage but only 20th in yards per attempt. The yardage rank is a product of attempts. His target tree is narrow. CeeDee Lamb has 27% of the targets at 0.746 EPA per target, while Jake Ferguson is a drain at -0.265.

What the totals hide is the gap between game states. In 157 plays within one score, he sits at 0.088 EPA per play, roughly average. When trailing by 9 or more, against softer coverage, he is at 0.602. The 0 interceptions in the red zone and 8 touchdowns there are excellent, but they come on 27 attempts. His bad-throw rate has climbed to 14.6%, 27th of 36, from 11.2% last season. The Tampa Bay game on four days' rest (-10 CPOE, 2 INT against the 5th-ranked defense) was the first time a good defense really tested him, and he didn't pass.

Going forward, the floor is sturdy: an offense ranked 4th in EPA, a pass-leaning staff and a defense that will keep forcing him to throw. The ceiling depends on Lamb's quad and on whether the accuracy wobble is a blip or the age-33 tax. Expect efficiency closer to top-15 than top-10, and a sack rate drifting back toward his career norms.

strengths.title: Intermediate and red-zone precision
strengths.body: The 10-19 yard window is where his offense lives: 0.487 EPA per attempt, with 5 of his 9 touchdowns there. Near the goal line he has 8 touchdowns and no interceptions. The intermediate efficiency matches a career built on timing throws, so it should hold. A 100% red-zone ball-security rate on 27 attempts will not.

strengths.title: Getting it out, not going down
strengths.body: He converts only 11.5% of pressures into sacks, 4th best, and his 3% sack rate ranks 3rd. That comes from a 2.7-second clock and a willingness to check down rather than hold the ball. The skill is real, but the degree isn't. His career pressure-to-sack rate usually sits in the 19-35% range, so some regression is coming.

strengths.title: The Lamb connection
strengths.body: Lamb's 52 targets at 0.746 EPA each make him the engine of the passing game. George Pickens adds a productive second option at 0.404. When Prescott can isolate Lamb, the offense plays at a top-five level. That is sustainable as long as Lamb is healthy.

concerns.title: Close-game efficiency is merely average
concerns.body: Most of his snaps come in one-score games, and there he is at 0.088 EPA per play with all 3 interceptions and all 6 sacks. The gaudy splits come when Dallas trails big against softer coverage. The leaky defense ensures that will keep happening, but it inflates the season line beyond his true level.

concerns.title: Accuracy slipping at 33
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate is 14.6%, 27th of 36. Last season it was 11.2%, 6th. The Tampa Bay game produced a -10 CPOE and two interceptions. He has had seasons like this before (2022, 2024) and rebounded, so it's a flag rather than a verdict. Still, it's the number most likely to decide whether he holds top-12 efficiency.

concerns.title: Thin beyond the top two
concerns.body: Ferguson's -0.265 EPA per target and the -0.333 EPA on throws behind the line mean the short game outside Lamb and Pickens is costing Dallas. If Lamb's quad lingers, the target share flows to the least efficient parts of the offense.

trend.note: He posted positive passing EPA of roughly 10-15 in each of the first four games against middling defenses. Then came a -3.3 against Tampa Bay's top-five unit on a short week. That reads as one bad matchup, not a slide, but it was the only real test.

nextGame.headline: A Lamb-friendly secondary inside a ceiling-capping defense
nextGame.body:
Green Bay has been tough on quarterbacks overall: it allows 12.4 PPR a game (3rd fewest) and the 2nd-lowest explosive pass rate. That caps the deep shots Prescott has been hitting on a small 17-attempt sample. The soft spot is the WR1 role. Top receivers have scored 4.8 PPR over their averages against Green Bay (26th) and posted 0.57 EPA per target (27th). That is exactly where Lamb lives. Meanwhile, GB's WR2 and WR3 coverage has been stingy, so this is a concentrated, short-to-intermediate game plan, not a spread-it-around one. An early forecast of 19 mph wind with 39 mph gusts is worth watching. It would push further in that direction, but it is days out.

Availability matters on both sides. Lamb (quad bruise, described as not serious) and right tackle Tyler Guyton (back, negative X-rays, 97% of snaps) are both questionable. Losing either would hit the two things propping up Prescott's profile: the WR1 target and the clean pocket. Green Bay has lost DT Javon Hargrave and LB Edgerrin Cooper, two regulars, and DT Anthony Campbell is out. That thins the interior rush and the second level that covers the middle. Micah Parsons is out, but he hasn't played this season, so GB's numbers already reflect his absence. Prescott also gets 10 days of rest after the 4-day turnaround that preceded his worst game.

keyMatchups.title: Lamb against GB's WR1 leak
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay has bled production to opposing top receivers, and Lamb is Prescott's most efficient target by a wide margin. If Lamb plays, expect a high target share. If he doesn't, the offense loses its best answer to this defense.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive-play suppression and wind
keyMatchups.body: GB allows explosive passes at the 2nd-lowest rate, and Prescott's deep-ball EPA rests on only 17 attempts. Add a possible gusty afternoon, and his yardage likely has to come in chunks of 8-15 yards, not shots.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted GB front vs. Guyton's back
keyMatchups.body: GB still sacks quarterbacks at the 9th-best rate, but losing Hargrave and Cooper weakens the interior and the underneath coverage. Whether Guyton plays decides if Prescott's elite sack avoidance survives this test.

nextGame.watch: Lamb's status and target share: with him, Prescott can attack GB's weakest coverage role; without him, the offense funnels to Ferguson and the screen game.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume should stay high. Dallas's pass defense is the worst in the league and the offense passes more than expected, so 260-290 yards a game is a reasonable baseline. His efficiency should settle closer to his 2025 line (around 0.19 EPA per play, top-15) than stay at the current number. Two things drive that: the red-zone and sack-avoidance rates will come back toward his career norms, and the one-score-game efficiency is ordinary.

Touchdown volume holds up because the offense is good and keeps chasing, but expect the occasional interception spike. A rising bad-throw rate and 10+ interceptions in five of his last six full seasons say the 1.6% interception rate is running light.
swingFactors: Whether the bad-throw rate settles back toward 2025 levels
Dallas defense continuing to force shootouts

bets.reason: Green Bay allows 219.2 passing yards a game to quarterbacks (7th fewest) and the 2nd-lowest explosive pass rate, which removes the chunk plays that pad his totals. Lamb is questionable, and the early wind forecast only adds to the case.

The market prices another Dallas shootout, and four of five Dallas games went over. But Green Bay's offense is middling (17th in EPA, worst rushing EPA) and is missing its center and a guard, while its defense suppresses big plays. The gusty forecast is a hedge-level bonus, not the case.

confidence.note: Five games, consistent with his career profile, but injury questions on Lamb and Guyton plus an early wind forecast cloud this week.
